KNOWN LIMITATION CANDIDATE: 'Grand Total (Rounded)  202.00' has a parenthetical between the label and the value; extractAmount's [^\d]* skip could plausibly stop early if OCR linearizes text unexpectedly. A mismatch here is a real finding, not a bad ground truth.

Marked 'Duplicate' at the top of the receipt; Name field is an unfilled placeholder (M: 0000000000), not real customer data.

Customer name line redacted (black bar) before committing.

KNOWN LIMITATION, CONFIRMED (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): the predicted date-format gap is independently verified by reading extractDate's regex (no hyphen-before-month-name support), but this specific receipt's date output is actually dominated by a separate, newly-discovered bug: extractDate's worded-date alternative (`\d{1,2}(st|nd|rd|th)?\s+[A-Za-z]+\s+\d{4}`) never checks that the middle token is a real month name, and `\s+` matches newlines -- so on this low-confidence (41%, lowest of all 21 entries) photo it false-positive-matched garbled text ("31\nPHO 1503") instead of returning no-date-found. Amount (42) was read correctly. Name field says 'CASH CUSTOMER' (generic, not real).

Separately, the date also mismatches: extracted "16-04-2028" vs ground truth 2026-04-16 is a single OCR digit misread (year's "6" read as "8") -- genuine source-image noise, not a regex defect (the numeric-date parser handled the matched text correctly).

Customer name, mobile, part of the bill number and part of the merchant address were already redacted with a physical yellow highlighter by the maintainer before this photo was taken/shared -- left as-is, not re-redacted digitally. NEW FINDING (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): extractDate's regex has no support for ISO-format (yyyy-mm-dd) dates and has no start-of-token anchor, so against the printed "2023-08-17" it matches a misleading substring starting at the year's 3rd digit -- "23-08-17" -- instead of the full date or no match at all, which downstream parses as 2017-08-23. This is a genuine, previously-undocumented production regex gap.
Clean single-total receipt; Name field unfilled. Has a 'CASH PAID' ink stamp overlapping part of the total block.

Indonesian Rupiah receipt -- comma is a thousands separator here ('107,000'), which happens to parse correctly through parseAmountInput's comma-stripping. 'Total Bill' (107,107, pre-rounding) and 'Grand Total' (107,000) both present; grand-total priority should select the right one. Guest name field says 'Umum' (Indonesian for 'general/public'), not a real name. CONFIRMED (real eval:ocr run, 2026-09-25): grand-total priority worked as intended, but Tesseract dropped a zero reading the printed amount, returning 10700 instead of 107000 -- genuine OCR digit-recognition noise on this photo (76% confidence), not a pipeline bug.
